amendments.body: Fix the snapshot TDS/conductivity projection so it is derived from the same fresh carbonate solve as the snapshot pH/CO2 values. In `crates/tank_core/src/types/snapshot.rs:78-90`, `TankSnapshot::from_state()` recomputes `carbonate_eq` from authoritative DIC + alkalinity, but `estimated_tds_7_ion_mg_per_l` / `estimated_conductivity_us_cm` still come from `chemistry.tds_mg_per_l()` and `chemistry.conductivity_us_cm()`. Those helpers read `WaterState::bicarbonate_mg_total` through `crates/tank_core/src/types/water.rs:189-240`, and that field is only a cache. If DIC/alkalinity changed without a preceding `resolve_carbonate_state()`, the snapshot can report internally inconsistent chemistry: fresh pH/CO2 with stale bicarbonate-backed TDS. Derive the bicarbonate contribution from `carbonate_eq.hco3_mmol_per_l` inside `TankSnapshot::from_state()` (or force a carbonate refresh before reading TDS), and add a regression test that mutates DIC/alkalinity while leaving the cache stale.
amendments.rationale: This is a correctness bug in the new chemistry surface. I reproduced it locally with a `TankState` whose DIC/alkalinity were changed without refreshing the cache: the snapshot pH updated to the new equilibrium, while the reported 7-ion TDS remained about 51.5 mg/L too high because it still used the old bicarbonate cache.

amendments.body: Centralize the 7-ion scope metadata next to the actual TDS calculation instead of maintaining separate hardcoded copies in core, API, and TUI. The authoritative ion set is implicit in `crates/tank_core/src/types/water.rs:235-242`, but the explanatory strings are duplicated in `crates/tank_api/src/handlers/snapshot.rs:8-12` / `crates/tank_api/src/handlers/snapshot.rs:121-125` and again in `crates/tank_tui/src/screens/mod.rs:11-15`. Move the tracked/omitted-ion metadata into `tank_core` and have both API and TUI consume that shared definition.
amendments.rationale: This bead’s main goal is honest user-facing chemistry semantics. Right now the number and the explanation come from different sources of truth, so a future ion addition/removal can silently make the API/TUI labels lie about what the 7-ion estimate actually contains.

payload.summary: `git diff` is clean in the worktree, so I reviewed the committed chemistry-semantics implementation directly and read the key core/API/TUI files end-to-end. I found one concrete correctness bug in snapshot TDS/conductivity derivation and one significant robustness risk from duplicated TDS-scope metadata.
